newsitem.title: USA: Networking fundamentals strong, fears near-term - H&Q.
newsitem.headline: Networking fundamentals strong, fears near-term - H&Q.

text.p: Hambrecht & Quist analyst Farrokh Billimoria said business fundamentals remain strong in the computer network equipment industry, but short-term concerns caused him to downgrade three leading network stocks Tuesday.
The analyst cut his ratings on Cicso Systems Inc, Cabletron Systems Inc and Fore Systems Inc. He cut Cisco and Cabletron to buy from strong buy and reduced Fore to neutral from buy.
"Fundamentals of the sector are healthy. Budgets continue to grow and network rollouts are on track," Billimoria said.
"There is stuff that's quite positive. It's just that it's a quarter away," the analyst said.
He said his worries about Cisco are tied to concerns about the company's revenue growth in its fiscal third and fourth quarters, especially from its Japanese business.

Billimoria cut his earnings estimates for Cisco's third quarter ending April to $0.52 a share from $0.54, and cut the fourth quarter to $0.55 from $0.58. He cut his fiscal 1998 estimate to $2.67 a share from $2.83.
On Fore, Billimoria said he is not optimistic that Fore can meet expectations for the current quarter.
He cut his outlook on earnings for Fore's fiscal fourth quarter to $0.14 a share from $0.15, and cut fiscal year 1998 to $0.73 from $0.80.

He predicted the traditionally back-loaded quarter could come up short and that days required to collect accounts receivable may return to traditional levels of around 76 or 77 days sales outstanding (DSOs) from last quarter's 72.

He also noted that Fore's Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) products face an increasing array of competing technologies, including gigabit Ethernet, Fast Ethernet and switching, and Japan's contribution to revenues is slowing.

The analyst believes the general challanges facing the networking industry will have some short-term impact on Cabletron, but he said Cabletron remains one of the better-positioned companies in the industry "and could emerge ahead of the game."
Cabletron's DSOs could be affected in the short-run, he said.

Although Cabletron has been able to stave off some of the worst of the sellling pressures seen in the networking sector this year, it is likely to be subject increasingly to some of these pressures in the short-term, he said.
